one_line: Neo-Vaishnava reformers of 15th–16th century Assam who reshaped devotion, art and community life through song, drama and the sattra–namghar institutions.

appearance.age_look: Sankaradeva appears as a wiry man in his late 60s–70s, still upright and energetic; Madhavdeva appears as a lean man in his late 40s–50s, slightly shorter but athletic.
appearance.face: Sankaradeva has an oval face with high cheekbones, medium brown Assamese complexion, fine horizontal forehead lines, a straight medium-length nose, neatly trimmed grey moustache and short beard along the jaw, watchful almond eyes with a calm, slightly smiling default expression; Madhavdeva has a slightly longer face, similar medium-brown tone, clean-shaven with a sharp jaw, straight nose and intense yet gentle eyes, his default expression earnest and quietly determined.
appearance.hair: Sankaradeva’s hair is mostly grey, gathered in a small, neat topknot high on the back of the head and covered by a plain off-white Assamese cloth turban wrapped low and flat; a few grey side-locks peek in front of the ears; Madhavdeva’s hair is black, also in a small topknot but usually hidden under a similar off-white turban with a slightly narrower wrap, with no loose strands.
appearance.costume: Both wear region- and era-accurate, modest Assamese Vaishnava attire: Sankaradeva in a full-sleeved, knee-length off-white cotton tunic (like a simple kurta) with side slits at the thigh, over an ankle-length cream dhoti wrapped in the Brahmaputra-valley style with neat pleats at the front, the dhoti border edged with a thin muted-red line; a soft, handwoven, pale-cream cotton gamosa with a simple red woven end pattern is draped over his left shoulder and across the torso; he is barefoot or in simple brown leather sandals, with minimal jewellery limited to a single small tulsi-bead necklace tightly at the neck; Madhavdeva wears a similar full-sleeved off-white tunic, slightly narrower at the wrists, over a slightly lighter cream dhoti with a subtle pale-yellow hue and a thin maroon border; his gamosa is worn more like a scarf around the neck, ends hanging in front; both tunics and dhotis are plain, unembellished homespun cotton, slightly creased from daily wear, with soft, flowing folds that read as realistic cloth; overall silhouettes are straight and modest, with no exposed torso or legs.
appearance.signature: Sankaradeva carries a long, slender palm-leaf manuscript bundle wrapped in a light-brown cloth and tied with a red cotton cord in his left arm, and keeps a simple, medium-brown wooden ekasarana-style walking staff in his right hand; Madhavdeva carries a medium-sized, light-brown one-sided khol frame drum slung at his left hip with a cream cloth strap, its body decorated only with a simple red-painted ring near each edge, and a single slim drumstick held in his right hand.

ref_desc: Srimanta Sankaradeva is a wiry, grey-haired Assamese elder with a small topknot under a flat off-white turban, off-white long tunic, cream-bordered dhoti, cream gamosa, tulsi necklace and wooden staff holding a wrapped palm-leaf manuscript, always beside Madhavdeva, a lean, clean-shaven Assamese man in an off-white tunic, pale-cream dhoti with maroon border, cream gamosa, off-white turban and a light-brown khol drum at his hip with a slim stick, both in muted off-whites, creams, maroons and light browns.
sheet_prompt: Draw an anime-style full-body model sheet of two consistent characters standing side by side: Srimanta Sankaradeva and Madhavdeva, late-medieval Assamese Neo-Vaishnava reformers. Sankaradeva is a wiry elder with medium-brown skin, oval face, high cheekbones, fine forehead lines, straight nose, neat grey moustache and short jawline beard, calm almond eyes and a gentle, slightly smiling expression; his grey hair is gathered in a small topknot hidden under a low, flat off-white cloth turban with a simple wrap and a few grey side-locks showing at the ears. He wears a modest, full-sleeved knee-length off-white cotton tunic with side slits and an ankle-length cream dhoti wrapped in Assamese style with neat front pleats and a thin muted-red border, plus a soft, pale-cream cotton gamosa with simple red patterns draped from left shoulder across the torso; he is barefoot or in simple brown sandals, with only a small tulsi-bead necklace. In his left arm he cradles a long, slender palm-leaf manuscript bundle wrapped in light-brown cloth tied with a red cord, and in his right hand he holds a plain medium-brown wooden walking staff. Beside him, Madhavdeva is a slightly shorter, lean, athletic man with similar medium-brown complexion, longer face, sharp jaw, straight nose, clean-shaven, with intense but kind eyes and an earnest expression; his black hair is in a small topknot under a slightly narrower off-white turban. He wears a full-sleeved off-white tunic and an ankle-length pale-cream dhoti with a faint pale-yellow tint and a thin maroon border, plus a cream gamosa around his neck with ends hanging in front. A light-brown one-sided khol drum hangs at his left hip on a cream cloth strap, the drum body marked only by a simple red ring near each edge; he holds a slim drumstick in his right hand. Show them in clean shonen-anime proportions with modest, draped garments, realistic cloth folds, no fantasy elements, and a restrained palette dominated by off-white, cream, muted red, maroon and light brown, front and slight-angle views to clearly show face, hair, full costume and their staff, manuscript and drum.
